questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (b).

Rule / Concept: Redundancy of Ability & Double Negatives –

In English grammar, the negative form of the modal "can" is used to express present inability or impossibility. Two major traps are frequently tested in banking and SSC exams:

Redundancy: Using "cannot" and "be able to" in the same clause is a "Superfluous Expression" error because both terms denote the same concept of ability.

Double Negatives: Adverbs like hardly, scarcely, and barely already contain a negative sense. Using them with "cannot" or "can't" creates a grammatically incorrect double negative.

options_en: are
being

Has been
options_hi: are
being
is
Has been
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (A)- The blank should be filled with the plural verb "are".

Rule/Concept: Adjectives Used as Nouns (The + Adjective) In English grammar, when the definite article "the" is placed before an adjective (like honest, poor, rich, blind, young, dead), the phrase functions as a plural noun. It refers to a whole group or class of people. Because it represents a group of individuals, it always takes a plural verb.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "The honest" does not mean one honest person; it means "honest people in general."

Why (C) is incorrect: "Is" is singular. While "honesty" (the abstract noun) takes a singular verb, "the honest" (the group of people) requires a plural verb.

Correct Sentence: ...it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest are rewarded for their integrity.

Tips:

The Group Rule: Always remember the formula: The + Adjective = Plural People.

The poor are... (Poor people)

The rich are... (Rich people)

The unemployed are... (Unemployed people)

Noun vs. Adjective: Do not confuse "The honest" with "Honesty."

Honesty is the best policy. (Abstract noun = Singular)

The honest are respected. (Group of people = Plural)

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Reading the controversial manuscript several
times, the editor finally realized that it
had the potential to be a bestseller.
No error
options_hi: Reading the controversial manuscript several
times, the editor finally realized that it
had the potential to be a bestseller.
No error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “Reading” with “Having read”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Perfect Participle

The Perfect Participle (Having + V3) is used to represent an action that was completed at some point in the past before another action took place. It emphasizes the completion of the first action as a prerequisite for the second.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"Reading the controversial manuscript several times..."

In this sentence, the editor first finished reading the manuscript multiple times, and only then did he realize its potential. Using the Present Participle ("Reading") implies that both actions (reading and realizing) were happening simultaneously. Since the realization is a result of the completed reading process, the Perfect Participle "Having read" must be used to show the chronological sequence.

Corrected Sentence

Having read the controversial manuscript several times, the editor finally realized that it had the potential to be a bestseller.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ Having finished her work, she went to the cinema.

Example 2 ✅ Having been warned before, he did not repeat the mistake.

Example 3 ✅ Having typed the letter, the clerk went to the manager for a signature.

questions.q_en:
Identify the noun clause in the sentence.

The director confirmed that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year, although several unexpected challenges had delayed the initial phase of construction.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the noun clause in the sentence.

The director confirmed that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year, although several unexpected challenges had delayed the initial phase of construction.
options_en: although several unexpected challenges had delayed the initial phase of construction
before the end of the financial year
that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year
The director confirmed
options_hi: although several unexpected challenges had delayed the initial phase of construction
before the end of the financial year
that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year
The director confirmed
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year

Explanation: A noun clause is a subordinate clause that functions as a noun in a sentence. It may act as a subject, object, or complement.

In this sentence, the clause:

“that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year” acts as the object of the verb “confirmed.”

confirmed what? → that the project would be completed before the end of the financial year

Therefore, it is a noun clause.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) This is an adverb clause because it begins with “although” and shows contrast.

B) This is a prepositional phrase, not a clause, because it lacks a subject-verb structure.

D) This is part of the main clause, not a noun clause.

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The young diplomat solemnly promised
that he would always endeavour doing
his absolute best for his country.
No Error
options_hi: The young diplomat solemnly promised
that he would always endeavour doing
his absolute best for his country.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “doing” with “to do”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Infinitives after Specific Verbs

Verbs that are followed by infinitive:- Seem, appear, decide, desire,

want, endeavor, stop, hurry, fail, happen, refuse, forget, remember,

promise, prove etc.

certain verbs are followed by an Infinitive (to + V1) to express a purpose, goal, or future action. The verb "Endeavour" (meaning to make an earnest effort) belongs to this group. When "endeavour" is used as the main verb, the action being attempted must be in the infinitive form. Using a Gerund (V{ing}) after these specific verbs is a common grammatical error.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...he would always endeavour doing his absolute best..."

In this sentence, "endeavour" is the primary verb indicating the effort. The action he is trying to perform is "doing." According to the rules of verb patterns, "endeavour" cannot take the $-ing$ form directly. It must be paired with the infinitive "to do."

Corrected Sentence

The young diplomat solemnly promised that he would always endeavour to do his absolute best for his country.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ We must endeavour to protect our environment for future generations.

Example 2 ✅ She refused to accept the bribe offered by the contractor.

Example 3 ✅ They hope to reach the summit before sunset.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The archaeologists carefully excavated the site for months,
documented every minor artifact they discovered, and
finally submit their findings to the Ministry of Culture.
No Error
options_hi: The archaeologists carefully excavated the site for months,
documented every minor artifact they discovered, and
finally submit their findings to the Ministry of Culture.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “submit” with “submitted”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Consistency of Tenses (Parallelism in Time)

In a sentence describing a sequence of actions that occurred in the past, all the verbs must remain in the Past Tense (V2) to maintain a logical and consistent timeline. If the narrative starts in the past (e.g., excavated, documented), it must continue in the past unless there is a specific reason to change the time frame.

Application to the Given Question

"...excavated the site... documented every minor artifact... and finally submit their findings..."

In this sentence, three distinct actions are performed by the archaeologists:

  1. They excavated (Past Tense - V2).

  2. They documented (Past Tense - V2).

  3. They submit (Present Tense - V1).

Since the first two actions establish that the event happened in the past, the final action in the sequence must also be in the past tense to maintain parallelism. Therefore, "submit" is chronologically inconsistent.

Corrected Sentence

The archaeologists carefully excavated the site for months, documented every minor artifact they discovered, and finally submitted their findings to the Ministry of Culture.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The committee members could not __________ the chairman’s proposal during the meeting.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The committee members could not __________ the chairman’s proposal during the meeting.
options_en: agree with
agree on
agree to
agree upon
options_hi: agree with
agree on
agree to
agree upon
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (1).

English Explanation: “Agree with” is used when we express having the same opinion as someone or something. In the sentence, the object is “the chairman’s proposal,” which refers to an idea/opinion. Therefore, “agree with” correctly conveys that the committee members did not share the same opinion about the proposal.

1. Agree with (किसी व्यक्ति या विचार से सहमत होना)

Example: I completely agree with your viewpoint. (मैं आपके दृष्टिकोण से पूरी तरह सहमत हूँ।)

2. Agree on (किसी बात पर सामूहिक निर्णय लेना)

Example: The team agreed on a new strategy. (टीम ने नई रणनीति पर सहमति बनाई।)

3. Agree to (किसी प्रस्ताव/अनुरोध को स्वीकार करना)

Example: She agreed to help me with the project. (उसने मेरी परियोजना में मदद करने के लिए सहमति दी।)

4. Agree upon (औपचारिक रूप से निर्णय लेना)

Example: The terms were agreed upon after negotiation. (बातचीत के बाद शर्तों पर औपचारिक सहमति हुई।)

Rule / Concept: Reflexive Pronouns with Transitive Verbs (Amuse) -

Certain transitive verbs in English, such as amuse, avail, absent, require an object to complete their meaning. If the subject is the receiver of the action and there is no other direct object mentioned, a reflexive pronoun (himself, herself, themselves, etc.) must be used. To "amuse" means to entertain someone; if you are the one being entertained by your own actions, you must "amuse yourself."

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the verb "amused" is used without an object. The child is the one performing the action of entertaining, and he is also the one being entertained. Because the sentence lacks a direct object (like "he amused his sister"), the reflexive pronoun "himself" (matching the subject "he") must be inserted to make the verb grammatically complete.

Corrected Sentence - During the long flight to London, the young child was so well-behaved that he amused himself with his coloring books and puzzles for nearly the entire duration of the journey.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with "Not only... but also"

When a sentence begins with the phrase "Not only", the first clause must undergo Partial Inversion. This means the auxiliary verb (is, are, was, were, do, does, did, has, have) is placed before the subject. However, the second part of the sentence (the "but also" part) follows the standard subject-verb order.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Not only is the newly appointed chief executive officer highly experienced...

In this sentence, "Not only" starts the sentence. The subject is "the newly appointed chief executive officer". The auxiliary verb "is" correctly precedes the subject, fulfilling the requirement for inversion. The second part of the sentence, "but she also possesses...", correctly maintains the standard subject-verb order. Therefore, the sentence is grammatically sound.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: Not only did he pass the exam, but he also topped the state.

Example 2 ✅: Not only has she completed the project, but she has also prepared the presentation.

Example 3 ✅: Not only do they play football, but they also excel in academics.

Rule / Concept: Partial Inversion after Negative Conjunctions

When a sentence or a clause begins with a negative word or conjunction like Nor, Neither, Scarcely, Hardly, Seldom, or Never, we must use Inversion.

Inversion means the Helping Verb (Auxiliary Verb) is placed before the Subject.

Application to the Given Question

The sentence contains two clauses. The second clause starts with the negative conjunction "nor":

"...nor (Negative Conjunction) her brother (Subject) has (Helping Verb)..."

According to the rule of inversion, since the clause starts with "nor," the helping verb "has" must jump in front of the subject "her brother."

Corrected Sentence

You will be surprised to know that she hasn’t apologized for her rude behaviour, nor has her brother.

More Examples for Clarity

  1. Neither/Nor: He doesn't like tea, nor does he like coffee. (Not: nor he likes)

  2. Hardly: Hardly had I reached the station when the train left. (Not: Hardly I had)

  3. Seldom: Seldom do we see such a magnificent performance. (Not: Seldom we do)

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Indefinite for Habitual Actions -

Actions that are habitual, regular, or repeated are traditionally expressed using the Simple Present Tense (Present Indefinite). While the Present Perfect (has gone) can sometimes show a recently completed action, the presence of a frequency adverb like "regularly" or "daily" coupled with a present state of being ("so he is very fit") strongly dictates the use of the Simple Present to show a permanent routine.

These adverbs of frequency represent habitual actions- Always, Often, Daily, Every day, Regularly, Frequently, Occasionally, Seldom, Never, etc.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this context, the sentence describes Rohan's ongoing lifestyle choice that results in his current fitness. The auxiliary "has" + past participle "gone" implies a completed action or a specific experience, which contradicts the nature of a "regular" habit. To show a recurring routine, we must use the V1 form (with 's/es' for third-person singular).

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 - She always drinks tea in the morning before starting her work. ✅

Example 2 - My father seldom watches television as he prefers reading journals. ✅

Example 3 - They regularly visit the orphanage to distribute books and clothes. ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 He is always coming late to the office every day. ❌ (Use: always comes)

Wrong example 2 I have often seen the sunset from this balcony every evening. ❌ (Use: often see)

Rule/Concept: Adjective after Noun when Preposition Follows -

When a noun is immediately followed by a prepositional phrase, any adjective describing that noun must come after the noun, not before.

Placing the adjective before the noun in such cases is considered grammatically incorrect in SSC CGL standards.

Application to the Given Question - Here, the noun “plan” is followed by the prepositional phrase “for the development of infrastructure…”. The adjective “comprehensive” is incorrectly placed before the noun. According to Rule, it must come after the noun.

Corrected Sentence -

The minister, after consulting various experts and reviewing multiple reports on regional development, presented a plan comprehensive for the development of infrastructure in rural districts, including roads, healthcare facilities, and educational institutions.

More Examples for Clarity -

A report detailed on environmental impacts → a report detailed on environmental impacts.

A strategy effective for improving literacy → a strategy effective for improving literacy.

A solution innovative for reducing pollution → a solution innovative for reducing pollution.

Incorrect Usage -

A plan comprehensive for urban development. (Incorrect placement in SSC trap style).

An initiative important for social welfare. (Adjective before noun, preposition follows).

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Always check if a prepositional phrase follows a noun; if yes, place the adjective after the noun.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Attributive Adjective vs. The Predicative Verb

Specific verbs possess two distinct forms for the Past Participle (V3): one used as a functional verb and the other as a descriptive adjective.

The Weak Form (-ed): Used in perfect tenses or passive voice to show an action.

Example: He had shaved just before the interview. (V_3 Verb)

The Strong/Ancient Form (-en): Used as an attributive adjective when placed directly before a noun to describe a state.

Example: He is a shaven man. (Adjective)

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word is not being used to describe the action of shaving; it is being used as an adjective to describe the appearance of the "face" (the noun).

When the participle is used in this attributive position (Adjective + Noun), formal grammar mandates the use of the adjectival form "shaven". Using "shaved" in this position is a common "Participle Error" that examiners use to trip up candidates who rely on casual, conversational English.

questions.solution_en:
Correction: Replace "must" with "had to"

The Rule: Tense Harmony and "Must" in the Past

According to the principle of tense consistency, if the Main Clause is in the Past Tense, the Subordinate Clause should also be in a past form.

While "must" is often used to express obligation in the present, it lacks a direct past-tense form. In indirect speech or complex sentences where the reporting verb is in the past (e.g., told, said, ordered), the obligation expressed by "must" generally shifts to "had to".

Exception: When "Must" stays "Must"

Examiners sometimes include "No Error" traps where "must" remains unchanged. This happens in two scenarios:

  1. Logical Deduction: If "must" is used to show a strong logical conclusion about the past (e.g., "The footprints must have been his").

  2. Universal Truths: If the sentence expresses a permanent rule or universal fact (e.g., "The teacher said that we must all die one day").

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Present Tense – Active to Passive Conversion
In the Simple Present Tense, the active structure is: Subject + V¹ / V¹+s + Object. The passive structure becomes: Object + am/is/are + V³ (+ by + Subject). The auxiliary verb (am/is/are) must agree with the new subject, and the main verb must be converted into its past participle (V³) form.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The internal audit committee scrutinizes the offshore accounts to ensure compliance with the new fiscal policy. Here, “scrutinizes” is in the simple present tense. “The offshore accounts” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is plural, the correct auxiliary is “are.” The verb “scrutinize” changes to its past participle form “scrutinized.” Hence, “are scrutinized” is the correct transformation.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Always match am/is/are with the new subject (singular/plural). Always convert the main verb to V³. Do not change the tense while converting. Keep purpose clauses unchanged.
